title: Crab Salad in Endive Leaves
ingredients: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, or as needed to bind
1/2 pound crabmeat, picked over and cartilage removed
Grated zest of 1 lemon plus 1 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
method: Stir the mayonnaise and mustard together in a large bowl.
Mix in the crab, celery, lemon zest and juice, chives and parsley.
Season with salt, black pepper and cayenne.
Cover and chill until serving; it keeps up to a day but is best within 6 hours.
Right before serving, spoon the salad onto the endive leaves and arrange on a platter.

title: Caviar and Cream Cheese Roll
ingredients: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus 1 to 2 tablespoons for buttering the pan
Freshly ground black pepper to taste
method: Heat the oven to 375°F. Butter a 10 x 15-inch jelly roll pan, line it with parchment and butter the paper.
Warm the milk. In another pan melt 4 tablespoons butter, whisk in flour, salt and pepper, then slowly whisk in the milk.
Simmer 2 to 3 minutes until thickened, then take off the heat and whisk in the beaten yolks a little at a time.
Beat the whites stiff; stir a third into the base, then gently fold in the rest.
Spread in the pan and bake 30 to 40 minutes until puffed and golden. Cover with a damp towel and cool about 10 minutes.
Mash the cream cheese with sour cream, work in 2 tablespoons of the roe, then fold in the rest and the chives if using.
Invert the cake onto the towel, peel off the parchment, spread with filling and roll up lengthwise using the towel.
Wrap and chill (up to 8 hours). Cut into 1-inch slices and garnish with watercress.

title: Crunchy Fried Mozzarella and Anchovy Sandwiches
ingredients: 12 slices baguette or rustic bread, cut about 3/4 inch thick
6 slices fresh mozzarella cheese, cut 1/2 inch thick
method: Spread 6 bread slices with chopped anchovy, top each with mozzarella and a second slice, and pin with toothpicks.
Set out three shallow bowls: flour, milk and beaten eggs.
Heat 3 inches of oil in a large saucepan to 365°F.
Coat each sandwich in flour, then milk, then egg, letting it soak in the egg 1 to 2 minutes.
Fry in batches, turning once, until golden, 4 to 5 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels, pull out the toothpicks, cut large ones into halves or quarters and serve hot.

title: Asian-Inspired Shrimp Salad
ingredients: 3 cups dry white wine or water or a combination
1 pound (about 16 to 20) large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes or diced jalapeño chile, or more to taste
2 ripe papayas or mangos, or 1 cantaloupe
method: Bring the wine (or water) to a simmer, add the shrimp and poach about 3 minutes until pink.
Lift out the shrimp and chill at least 1 hour (up to a day); discard the liquid.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and zest, brown sugar and pepper flakes; season with salt and more heat if you like.
Peel, seed and dice or slice the papaya, mango or cantaloupe.
Combine the lettuces, mint and basil in a big bowl.
Toss the shrimp with 1/4 cup vinaigrette and let sit 5 minutes.
Dress the greens with half the remaining vinaigrette, plate, top with shrimp and fruit, and drizzle with the rest.

title: Grilled, Herb-Marinated Fish on a Bed of White Beans
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 6-ounce fillets of albacore tuna, swordfish, or sea bass
method: Simmer the oil with thyme, sage, bay and rosemary over medium heat, then 2 to 3 minutes on low to infuse.
Cool to lukewarm, stir in garlic, orange zest, salt and pepper, and let cool fully. Set aside 2 tablespoons.
Pour the rest over the fish in a shallow dish and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
Heat a grill or broiler. Lift the fish from the marinade and season with salt and pepper.
Cook about 3 to 4 minutes per side, until opaque in the centre.
Spoon warm white beans onto plates, top with fish, drizzle with the reserved marinade, add pepper and serve with lemon.
protein: albacore tuna, swordfish or sea bass

title: Cooked White Beans
ingredients: 1/2 pound (1 cup) dried cannellini, great northern, or other white beans
3 whole sage leaves or 1 bay leaf
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
method: Soak the beans overnight in 1 quart water in the fridge, or boil them 2 minutes in 2 quarts water, cover off the heat and let stand 1 hour.
Drain, cover with 1 quart fresh cold water and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the whole sage leaves (plus onion and whole garlic if using), turn heat low, skim, cover and simmer 40 to 60 minutes until tender; salt after 15 minutes.
Discard the aromatics and drain, keeping the beans in about 1 cup of their liquid.
Toss the warm beans with 3 tablespoons oil and season. They keep up to 2 days refrigerated.
Gently cook the minced garlic in the remaining 2 tablespoons oil about 3 minutes, add the beans with liquid and chopped sage, and simmer 15 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and finish with a drizzle of oil.

title: Roast Lobster with Tarragon-Lemon Butter
ingredients: 1/2 pound (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Boil the lobsters in a very large pot of well-salted water for 7 to 8 minutes, then plunge into ice water.
Split each lobster lengthwise, remove the head sac, and pick out claw and body meat in bite-size pieces.
Pile the meat back into the body shells, wrap and refrigerate.
Boil vinegar, shallot and tarragon about 5 minutes until syrupy and nearly gone; add lemon juice and zest and cool.
Beat the butter in a food processor until creamy, blend in the tarragon mixture and season.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Spread the butter over the lobster meat, cover loosely with foil and roast 8 minutes. Serve at once.

title: Polenta with Smoked Fish and Crème Fraîche
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups fresh corn kernels (from about 2 ears of corn), or 1 1/2 cups frozen corn kernels (optional)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 medium red onions, cut in 1/4-inch slices
12 ounces smoked trout fillets, broken into 2-inch pieces (from about 2 trout), or 12 ounces smoked salmon, cut into 2 x 1/2–inch strips
method: If using corn, boil the kernels 1 to 2 minutes, drain and pat very dry.
Oil a small baking sheet. Bring cornmeal and 4 cups cold water to a boil, then cook on low, stirring often, about 30 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir in the corn, season, spread on the sheet and chill about 2 hours until firm (can be made a day ahead).
Cook the onions in butter over medium heat 10 minutes, then low heat 10 minutes more until golden.
Cut the polenta into 8 triangles or strips and grill or broil about 5 minutes total, turning once (or warm 10 minutes in a 350°F oven).
Plate the polenta, top with smoked fish and onions, drizzle with crème fraîche and sprinkle with chives.

title: Baked Ricotta with Toast
ingredients: 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, or as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 300°F and oil a 4-cup crock or soufflé dish.
Stir the ricotta with salt, pepper and herbs if using.
Pack it into the dish and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake about 15 minutes, until warm and slightly wobbly.
Let cool a few minutes and serve with grilled or toasted bread.

title: Pasta with Greens, Chickpeas, Toasted Breadcrumbs, and Pecorino
ingredients: 8 cups escarole, chard, or arugula, cut into 1-inch strips and washed, or 1 large bunch broccoli rabe, washed and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 cup cooked chickpeas or white beans (see recipe on page 58), or drained canned chickpeas or white beans
method: Boil the greens in a large pot of salted water 8 to 10 minutes until tender; lift out, cool under cold water and drain.
Return the water to a boil and cook the pasta over high heat until al dente, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile warm the oil on low and cook the garlic, anchovy and pepper flakes 2 minutes.
Add the greens and cook 3 to 5 minutes, then stir in chickpeas, half the breadcrumbs, lemon zest, pepper and some cheese for 1 minute.
Save 1 cup pasta water, drain the pasta and toss it with the greens, loosening with pasta water if dry.
Toss in the remaining breadcrumbs if you like and serve in warm bowls with the rest of the cheese on the side.

title: Toasted Breadcrumbs
ingredients: 2 cups cubed crustless day-old Italian or French bread
method: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Pulse the bread in a food processor into coarse crumbs.
Toss the crumbs with the oil, salt and pepper and spread on a baking sheet.
Bake about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until evenly golden.
Cool and store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days.

title: Calamari with Garlic and Peas
ingredients: 3 pounds peas in the pod (about 3 cups shelled)
3 ripe tomatoes, peeled, seeded, and chopped, or 1 1/2 cups chopped canned tomatoes (see note below)
1/3 cup dry white wine, or more as needed
1 1/2 pounds squid, cleaned and cut into 3/4-inch rings
method: Shell the peas and boil 3 to 5 minutes until tender; drain and rinse with cold water.
Fry the garlic in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until pale gold; remove. Fry the bread and almonds in the same oil about 5 minutes until golden; drain.
Cook the onion in the oil about 8 minutes until soft, then add the tomatoes and 1/3 cup wine and bring to a simmer.
Grind the fried garlic, almonds and bread to a paste (picada) in a mortar or food processor and stir it into the sauce with half the parsley and mint.
Simmer on low about 10 minutes; keep it saucy, adding water or wine if it gets thick.
Raise the heat to medium-high, add the squid and peas and cook 1 to 2 minutes until the squid turns opaque.
Serve sprinkled with the remaining mint and parsley.

title: Seafood Salad
ingredients: 1/2 pound squid, cleaned and cut into 1/2-inch pieces, tentacles separated
1/2 pound medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/2 cup dry white wine or water
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 to 5 celery stalks, thinly sliced, cut on the diagonal
method: Boil the squid in salted water 1 to 2 minutes until opaque; rinse cold and put in a large bowl.
Boil the shrimp in the same water 2 to 4 minutes until pink; rinse cold and add to the squid.
Discard any open clams or mussels that won't close. Steam the rest with the wine, covered, over medium-high heat 3 to 5 minutes, removing them as they open.
Discard any clams still shut after 10 minutes. Shell the cooled clams and mussels and add to the bowl.
Whisk the oil and lemon juice with a little salt, pepper and the pepper flakes if using.
Toss the seafood with the celery and dressing, sprinkle with parsley and serve at room temperature.

title: Baked Goat Cheese in a Walnut Crust with Greens and Apple
ingredients: 4 2-ounce rounds of fresh mild goat cheese, each about 1 inch thick, or 1 8-ounce log, cut into 1-inch rounds
1 to 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, or as needed
1/2 cup walnuts, toasted and finely chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tart green apple (such as Pippin or Granny Smith)
method: Coat the cheese rounds with olive oil and leave at room temperature 30 minutes.
Mix the chopped walnuts, breadcrumbs and thyme; press the mixture onto all sides of the cheese and set on a parchment-lined sheet.
Whisk the walnut oil, olive oil and both vinegars with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Toast the walnut halves about 8 minutes, chop coarsely and toss with a little vinaigrette.
Bake the cheese about 10 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Toss the greens with all but 3 tablespoons of the vinaigrette and divide among plates.
Top with thin unpeeled apple slices drizzled with the reserved dressing, the walnuts, and 1 or 2 warm cheese rounds. Serve at once.

title: Roast Pork Loin with Creamy Onion Sauce and Sautéed Apples
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/4 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg, or more to taste
method: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cut small slits all over the pork and push in the garlic slivers; season with salt and pepper.
Roast until an instant-read thermometer reads 140°F, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile cook both onions very slowly in 4 tablespoons butter over low heat 30 to 40 minutes until soft and sweet.
Separately cook the leeks in 2 tablespoons butter, covered, on low about 20 minutes until tender.
Puree onions and leeks, thin with stock, and season with nutmeg, salt and pepper; add cream if you like.
Brown the apple slices in the last 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat about 10 minutes.
Slice the pork between the bones, spoon on the sauce, scatter chives and serve with the apples.

title: Chinese Chicken Salad
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Vegetable oil for frying (such as canola or olive oil)
3 tablespoons finely minced peeled fresh ginger
1 1/2 cups vegetable oil (such as canola, peanut, or grapeseed oil)
1 large cucumber, peeled, seeded, and cut on the diagonal into 1/4-inch slices
1/4 cup minced green onions (mostly green parts)
method: Pound the chicken to an even thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Fry in 1/4 inch of hot oil over medium-high heat, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Drain, cool and shred.
For the dressing, puree garlic and ginger, add mustard, sugar, soy, vinegar and sesame oil, then slowly blend in the vegetable oil until emulsified. Salt to taste.
Toss the chicken and cucumber with at least 1/2 cup dressing.
Toss the romaine, sprouts, green onions and cilantro with another 1/2 cup dressing and divide among plates.
Top with the chicken mixture, drizzle with more dressing if wanted and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Refrigerate leftover dressing.

title: Tandoori-Style Shrimp
ingredients: 2 jalapeño chiles (leave seeds in for extra heat), chopped
2-inch piece of peeled fresh ginger, sliced thinly across the grain
1 1/2 pounds large shrimp, shelled and deveined
method: Pulse the yogurt, jalapeños, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, cumin, salt and turmeric in a food processor.
Toss the shrimp with the marinade in a nonaluminum container and refrigerate 1 hour.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes.
Heat a broiler or grill. Thread the shrimp onto pairs of parallel skewers.
Cook about 2 minutes per side, until pink and firm.
Dust with paprika and serve with lime or lemon wedges.

title: Baked Rockfish with Spicy Peanut Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 cup coconut milk, or more as needed
1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or more to taste
method: Put the peanut butter, peanuts and brown sugar in a small saucepan and gradually stir in stock, 1/2 cup coconut milk, soy, lemon juice, garlic, pepper flakes, cumin and coriander.
Bring to a boil and simmer on low 2 minutes. Adjust heat and thin to heavy-cream consistency with coconut milk or water. Keeps a week chilled.
Heat the oven to 450°F.
Mash the garlic, salt and pepper together and rub over the fillets; lay them in one layer in an oiled baking dish.
Spoon half the sauce over the fish and bake 10 to 15 minutes, until firm and opaque at the thickest part.
Serve with a little more warm sauce spooned over.
protein: rockfish (or halibut, sea bass, ling cod)

title: Butternut Squash Risotto with Gorgonzola Cheese
ingredients: 3 cups peeled butternut squash cut in 3/4-inch cubes
3 ounces crumbled Gorgonzola dolcelatte or other mild, creamy blue cheese
method: Keep the broth at a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Melt the butter with the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and cook onion, garlic and sage 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the squash with a little salt for 1 minute, then the rice, stirring about 3 minutes until opaque.
Add the wine if using and cook about 3 minutes until it evaporates.
Lower the heat and add broth a ladle (about 1 cup) at a time, stirring until absorbed, about 20 minutes total, until creamy and al dente.
Stir in the cream, Gorgonzola, 4 tablespoons Parmesan and walnuts if using; simmer about 2 minutes until melted.
Season and serve at once topped with the remaining Parmesan.

title: Scallop Ceviche with Grapefruit and Avocado
ingredients: 2 jalapeño chiles, seeded and minced (leave seeds in for extra heat)
3 tablespoons minced fresh mint or coriander (cilantro)
1 teaspoon salt, or more to taste
method: Trim the side muscles off the scallops and put them in a nonreactive dish.
Cover with the lime and grapefruit juices and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours.
Stir in the onion, jalapeños, oil, mint or cilantro, ginger if using and 1 teaspoon salt; marinate 1 hour more.
Fold in the grapefruit sections and avocado, adjust the salt and serve right away.

title: Moroccan-Inspired Fish with Olives and Lemon
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds fillets of white fish such as halibut, snapper, cod, sole, flounder, or sea bass
1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, or as needed
2 juicy lemons, peeled and seeded, sliced into paper-thin rounds
2/3 cup cured green olives, pitted and halved
method: Heat the oven to 475°F and lay the fish in one layer in an oiled baking dish.
Simmer the 1/4 cup water, take off the heat, add the saffron and steep 10 minutes.
Mash the garlic, cumin, salt and pepper with enough oil to make a paste and rub it over the fish.
Cover with lemon slices, pressing to release a little juice, then scatter on olives and cilantro and spoon over the saffron water.
Drizzle generously with oil and add stock to a depth of 1/4 inch.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes, until opaque at the thickest point.

title: Bouillabaisse-Style Seafood Stew
ingredients: 2 leeks, cut in half lengthwise, sliced crosswise into 1/4-inch pieces, well washed
2 to 3 strips orange zest, 1/2 x 3 inches each
8 to 9 cups Fish Stock (see recipe below)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 1/2 pounds firm white fish such as monkfish, flounder, bass, or snapper, cut into 2-inch pieces
3 lobsters, about 1 1/2 pounds each, boiled for 8 minutes, or 2 large crabs, boiled for 12 to 15 minutes, cleaned, cut into chunks with the shells on, and cracked where needed (optional)
2 to 3 pounds mussels, scrubbed and debearded
2 fennel bulbs, quartered, cored, and parboiled until tender (optional)
1/2 cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley for garnish
1/4 cup chopped fennel fronds for garnish
24 slices toasted French bread, rubbed with garlic
2 cups Aïoli or 1 cup Rouille (see recipes below)
method: Bring the 1/4 cup wine to a simmer, take off the heat, add saffron and steep 10 minutes.
Cook the leeks, onions, celery, garlic and orange zest in the oil over medium heat about 10 minutes until soft.
Add the saffron wine, fish stock, tomatoes, thyme, bay, ground fennel and pepper flakes; bring to a gentle boil and simmer on low 15 to 20 minutes. Season. (Base keeps 2 days chilled.)
To serve, simmer the base, add the fish and any lobster or crab for 2 to 3 minutes, then the shrimp and scallops for 3 to 4 minutes more until firm and opaque.
Steam the mussels in 1/2 inch of white wine, covered over high heat, 3 to 5 minutes; discard any unopened after 10 minutes.
Add the mussels and their strained liquid to the stew, plus the cooked fennel if using.
Top with parsley and fennel fronds and serve with garlic toasts and plenty of aïoli or rouille.

title: Aïoli
ingredients: Pinch of salt, or more to taste
2 cups mild olive oil, or part canola oil and part olive oil
method: Grind the garlic to a smooth paste with a pinch of salt in a mortar.
Blend the egg yolks with 3 tablespoons lemon juice in a blender or food processor.
With the motor running, add the oil a few drops at a time until thick and emulsified.
Mix in the garlic paste and more lemon juice and salt to taste; thin with a little water if needed.

title: Simple Rouille
method: Stir the tomato paste and cayenne into the aïoli until evenly blended.

title: Alternate Rouille
method: Put the bread, garlic, cayenne, olive oil and tomato paste in a food processor and blend.
Add fish stock little by little until the sauce is spoonable.

title: Fish Stock
ingredients: 6 to 8 pounds fish frames with heads and tails (from mild-flavored fish such as snapper, rockfish, or halibut), gills removed
2 quarts water, or more as needed
method: Rinse the fish frames well.
Cook the frames in the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat, stirring often, about 10 minutes until they release some liquid.
Add the water, wine, onions, celery, parsley, lemon zest, thyme, all the spices and bay, plus fennel seeds if using; add water to cover if needed.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered 30 minutes, skimming now and then.
Strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Chill covered up to 2 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 pound Fontina Val d’Aosta or Gruyère cheese, or a combination of the two
1 teaspoon cornstarch, arrowroot, or potato starch
Vegetable strips (such as fennel and carrots)
12 ounces Fontina Val d’Aosta or Fontal cheese
1 teaspoon cornstarch dissolved in 2 tablespoons wine
1/2 teaspoon truffle oil or shavings of white truffle (optional)
method: Choose either the Swiss-style (cheese melted in wine) or Italian-style fonduta (cheese soaked in milk, enriched with butter and egg yolks).
Swiss: Whisk 1/4 cup of the wine with the starch. Rub the top of a double boiler with the cut garlic.
Swiss: Heat the remaining 1 1/4 cups wine in the double boiler with the garlic, then whisk in half the cheese gradually until melted and bubbly.
Swiss: Whisk in the starch mixture, then the rest of the cheese, whisking until smooth. Season with pepper and nutmeg if you like.
Fonduta: Remove the rind, dice the cheese and soak it in the milk overnight in the fridge or 2 hours at room temperature.
Fonduta: Melt the butter in the top of a double boiler over simmering water and add the cheese and milk, whisking.
Fonduta: Keep whisking while adding the wine and the cornstarch mixture, then whisk in the yolks one at a time.
Fonduta: Cook 6 to 8 minutes until smooth and creamy, then stir in truffle oil or shavings if using.
Serve either version in a fondue pot over a warmer with vegetables and bread for dipping.

title: Swiss-Style Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 pound Fontina Val d’Aosta or Gruyère cheese, or a combination of the two
1 teaspoon cornstarch, arrowroot, or potato starch
Vegetable strips (such as fennel and carrots)
method: Remove the rind and dice the cheese.
Whisk 1/4 cup of the wine with the starch. Rub the top of a double boiler with the cut garlic.
Heat the remaining 1 1/4 cups wine in the double boiler with the garlic, then whisk in half the cheese gradually until melted and bubbly.
Whisk in the starch mixture, then the rest of the cheese, whisking until smooth. Season with pepper and nutmeg if you like.
Move to a fondue pot over a warmer and serve with vegetable strips and bread.

title: Italian-Style Cheese Fondue (Fonduta)
ingredients: 12 ounces Fontina Val d’Aosta or Fontal cheese
1 teaspoon cornstarch dissolved in 2 tablespoons wine
1/2 teaspoon truffle oil or shavings of white truffle (optional)
method: Remove the rind, dice the cheese and soak it in the milk overnight in the fridge or 2 hours at room temperature.
Melt the butter in the top of a double boiler over simmering water and add the cheese and milk, whisking.
Keep whisking while adding the wine and the cornstarch mixture, then whisk in the yolks one at a time.
Cook 6 to 8 minutes until smooth and creamy, then stir in truffle oil or shavings if using.
Transfer to a fondue pot over a warmer and serve with fennel, carrots and toasted bread or breadsticks.
wines: Gewürztraminer (New World; aged European if truffled)

title: Savory Meat Strudel
serves: 2 strudels serve 8 as a main course or 16 as an appetizer
ingredients: 1 pound ground veal, or part veal and part pork
Salt and lots of freshly ground black pepper
method: Soak the currants in hot water 30 minutes, then drain.
Cook the onion in 3 tablespoons butter over medium heat about 10 minutes, add garlic, thyme, cinnamon and nutmeg for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the meat and cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until lightly browned. Off the heat mix in currants, parsley, pine nuts, breadcrumbs and egg; season well and chill.
Clarify the stick of butter: melt on low, skim the foam and pour off the clear butter, leaving the milky solids.
Stack 6 phyllo sheets, brushing each with clarified butter. Lay half the filling in a strip 1 inch from a long edge, tuck in the ends and roll up. Repeat.
Set seam side down on a baking sheet. (Can be frozen up to 1 month; bake from frozen, adding 15 minutes.)
Bake at 350°F about 40 minutes until golden. Slice on the diagonal and serve with sour cream and chives.

title: Salmon with Spiced Onions and Currants
ingredients: 6 tablespoons olive oil or butter plus extra for buttering baking dishes
4 yellow onions, sliced into 1/4-inch rings (about 6 cups)
1/2 teaspoon salt plus additional as needed
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper plus additional as needed
method: Soak the currants in the cognac and hot water for 30 minutes.
Warm the oil or butter over medium heat, lower the heat, add the onions and cook about 20 minutes until very soft and sweet.
Add the cinnamon, nutmeg and currants with their liquid and cook about 5 minutes; season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Butter individual gratin dishes and divide the onions among them.
Set a salmon fillet on each, season lightly and spoon the stock over.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes depending on thickness, until done.

title: Duck with Orange Sauce
ingredients: 1 5-pound duck, neck, feet, wings, and excess fat removed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 whole oranges plus additional orange segments for garnish
4 tablespoons (1/2 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature, plus 1 tablespoon for binding the sauce
1/2 cup poultry broth, or more as needed
1 1/2 teaspoons sugar, or more to taste
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Season the duck inside and out, stuff with 1 quartered orange and close the cavity.
Brown the duck on all sides in 4 tablespoons butter and the oil in a Dutch oven over high heat, up to 25 minutes. Pour off the fat.
Deglaze with the grappa, add the wine, cover and braise in the oven about 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Cut the zest of a second orange into fine strips; blanch 3 minutes, drain and repeat once. Juice the last 2 oranges (about 3/4 cup).
Remove the duck and skim the fat. Add 1/2 cup broth and the juice, boil 8 to 10 minutes to 1 1/2 cups, then lower the heat and add the sugar.
Mash the last tablespoon butter with the flour and whisk in bit by bit to thicken. Add the zest and simmer 5 minutes; season.
Quarter the duck, discarding the orange inside, and serve with the sauce and orange segments.

title: Ginger and Orange Fried Chicken
ingredients: 12 small boneless, skinless chicken breast halves
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Trim the tendons from the chicken and pound the breasts to an even thickness.
Season the buttermilk with orange zest, fresh ginger, salt and pepper; add the chicken and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Mix the flour, curry powder, ground ginger, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon pepper and cayenne in a bowl or paper bag.
Heat 3 inches of oil in a deep pan to 365°F.
Shake off the excess buttermilk and coat each piece in the seasoned flour.
Fry 4 to 6 minutes per side, turning once, until golden; lower the heat if browning too fast.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Halibut with Orange and Mint Salsa Verde
ingredients: 1/4 cup very finely diced red or sweet white onion
2/3 cup thinly sliced fresh mint leaves
3 to 4 tablespoons lemon juice to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Olive oil, wine, or fish stock for cooking
method: Whisk the onion, mint, orange zest, olive oil, orange and lemon juices and salt. It can wait 2 to 3 hours chilled; bring back to room temperature.
To bake: season the fish, put in an oiled dish and bake at 450°F for 10 to 15 minutes until opaque in the thickest part.
Or to grill or broil: brush with oil, season and cook about 4 minutes per side.
Or to poach: bring 2 inches of wine, stock or water to a boil, drop to a bare simmer and poach covered about 7 minutes; drain on a towel.
Plate the fish, stir the sauce and spoon it over.

title: Brazilian Fish and Shellfish Stew
ingredients: 2 green bell peppers, seeded and chopped
2 to 3 jalapeño chiles or other hot peppers to taste, finely minced
1 1/2 cups drained canned tomatoes, chopped, or 3 fresh ripe tomatoes, peeled, seeded, and diced
1/2 cup canned cream of coconut (such as Coco Lopez), or more to taste
2 tablespoons lemon or lime juice, or more to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 1/2 pounds fish fillets (such as monkfish, snapper, rock cod, or flounder), cut into 2-inch pieces
method: Simmer the 1/4 cup wine, take off the heat, add the saffron and steep 10 minutes.
Melt the butter in a wide, deep pot over medium heat and cook the onions about 8 minutes until translucent.
Add bell peppers, jalapeños, garlic and ground coriander and cook about 5 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add the stock, tomatoes, 1/2 cup cream of coconut, 6 tablespoons cilantro and the saffron wine; simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in the lemon or lime juice, season, and balance sweet and sour with more coconut cream or juice.
Add the fish and clams, cover and simmer 2 minutes; add shrimp and mussels for about 2 minutes; then scallops for about 2 minutes more until shells open and scallops are opaque.
Discard any clams not open after 10 minutes. Serve over rice topped with the remaining cilantro and toasted coconut.

title: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Raisins, Almonds, and Honey
ingredients: 3 pounds lamb shoulder, trimmed well and cut into 2 1/2-inch pieces
2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, or more to taste
1/2 cup dark honey, or to taste
method: Mix the pepper, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and the other ground spices and saffron with 1/2 cup water to a paste.
Rub half over the lamb and refrigerate overnight; cover and chill the remaining paste.
Soak the raisins in hot water 30 minutes, then stir in the reserved paste and let stand 1 hour.
Put the lamb, melted butter, onions, garlic and cinnamon sticks in a Dutch oven with water just to cover.
Bring to a gentle boil, skim, then cover and simmer on low about 1 hour 15 minutes until nearly tender, adding water as needed.
Add the raisins with their liquid, the almonds, 1/2 cup honey and the remaining cinnamon.
Simmer, stirring often, 15 to 30 minutes until the sauce is a syrupy glaze. Adjust the cinnamon to taste.

title: Steak au Poivre
ingredients: 4 filets of beef, each about 1 1/2 inches thick
2 teaspoons kosher salt, plus salt for pan
2 or 3 tablespoons coarsely cracked black pepper
method: Rub each filet with about 1/2 teaspoon salt and press cracked pepper firmly into both sides.
Let the steaks sit at room temperature 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Whisk the wine, brandy, mustard and Worcestershire together.
Lightly film a heavy skillet with salt, heat on high, then melt in the butter and oil.
Sear the steaks on both sides, then cook over medium, about 3 to 4 minutes per side for rare. Move to a warm platter.
Pour the wine mixture into the pan and boil until reduced by half; whisk in cream if you want it smoother.
Spoon the sauce over the steaks and serve.

title: Spanish Lamb Ragout with Roasted Sweet Peppers
ingredients: 3 pounds lamb shoulder, fat and sinew trimmed, cut into 2-inch cubes, or 6 small lamb shanks
1 tablespoon sweet paprika or pimentón de la Vera (Spanish smoked paprika)
1/2 cup mild olive oil, or more as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons sweet paprika or pimentón de la Vera
method: Char the peppers on all sides under the broiler or over a flame, rest them covered 30 minutes, then peel, seed and cut into wide strips.
For the marinade, mix 1 tablespoon paprika, 2 teaspoons cumin and the bay leaf, whisk in 1/2 cup wine and 1/4 cup extra virgin oil, and pour over the lamb. Refrigerate overnight.
Bring the lamb to room temperature, lift from the marinade and pat dry.
Season and brown the lamb in batches in 1/4 cup mild oil over high heat, 8 to 10 minutes; move to a large pot.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining oil and cook the onions over medium about 10 minutes; add garlic, 2 tablespoons paprika and 2 teaspoons cumin for 2 minutes, season and add to the lamb.
Deglaze the pan with 1/2 cup wine and add to the pot with the stock whisked with tomato paste.
Bring to a gentle boil, cover and simmer on low about 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add the pepper strips and simmer 15 minutes more; season and garnish with parsley and olives.

title: Lamb Steaks with Greek-Inspired Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 4 3/4-inch-thick lamb steaks (8 to 10 ounces per steak), or 12 lamb loin chops (about 6 ounces per chop)
1 bunch green onions (including tender green tops), chopped
1 cup meat stock or dry red wine
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Whisk the wine, oil, oregano, pepper and cinnamon and pour over the lamb laid in one layer.
Marinate overnight in the fridge or 1 to 2 hours at room temperature; bring to room temperature before cooking.
For the sauce, cook the green onions in 1/4 cup oil over medium heat about 5 minutes, then the garlic, cinnamon and oregano about 5 minutes more.
Add the tomato sauce and stock or wine, bring to a gentle boil, then simmer on low about 8 minutes.
Season, and add a little honey or sugar if the sauce tastes too sharp.
Pat the lamb dry and broil about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Plate, spoon the sauce over and sprinkle with parsley.
protein: lamb leg steaks or loin chops

title: Coffee- and Pepper-Rubbed Rib Roast
method: Cut small slits all over the roast and push in the garlic slivers; set in a roasting pan.
Whisk the soy sauce and mustard, add the pepper and coffee, then slowly beat in the oil.
Spread the paste over the roast and leave at room temperature 1 to 2 hours.
Roast at 450°F for 15 minutes, then lower to 350°F.
Roast about 1 1/2 hours more, to 115°F on a meat thermometer for very rare (it rises about 10 degrees while resting).
Rest 15 to 20 minutes before carving.

title: Roast Cornish Hens Stuffed with Pork and Prunes
ingredients: 8 plump cloves garlic, minced, plus additional for seasoned butter
2 teaspoons chopped fresh thyme, plus additional for seasoned butter
1 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg, plus additional for seasoned butter
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Soak the prunes in the Armagnac for 1 hour.
Cook the onions in 4 tablespoons butter over medium heat about 8 minutes, then the celery and 8 cloves garlic about 3 minutes more.
Brown the pork in the olive oil over medium heat, stirring, about 10 minutes until no longer pink.
Mix in the onion mixture, the prunes with their liquid, 2 teaspoons thyme and 1 teaspoon nutmeg; season.
Heat the oven to 500°F. Melt the remaining butter and season it with salt, pepper, garlic, thyme and nutmeg.
Stuff and close the hens, season, and set on a rack in a roasting pan.
Roast 15 minutes, then at 400°F about 30 minutes more until the juices run clear, basting a few times with the butter.
Remove the string, halve each bird lengthwise and serve two halves per plate, stuffing side up.

title: Tuna with Rosemary and Citrus Tapenade
ingredients: 1 tablespoon olive oil, or as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Whisk the olives, rosemary, orange zest, garlic and 1/2 teaspoon pepper, then whisk in the lemon juice, orange juice and 1/2 cup oil.
If made ahead, refrigerate and bring back to room temperature before cooking the fish.
Heat a broiler or grill.
Brush the tuna with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, turning once, until browned.
Plate the fish, rewhisk the tapenade and spoon it over.

title: Catalan Bean and Sausage Stew with Mint
ingredients: 2 cups dried white beans or dried favas
2 teaspoons salt, or more to taste
4 chorizo, botifarra, or other fresh spicy sausages (about 1 pound, not encased in plastic)
1/4 pound salt pork or bacon, diced
3 tomatoes, peeled, seeded, and chopped, or 1 1/2 cups canned chopped tomatoes, drained
1 tablespoon sweet paprika or pimentón de la Vera
1/2 cup meat stock or water, or more as needed
3 tablespoons chopped fresh mint plus additional for garnish
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Soak the beans overnight in cold water in the fridge, or boil 2 minutes in 2 quarts water and let stand covered 1 hour. Drain and rinse.
Cover with cold water by 2 inches, add 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves and the bay leaf, bring to a boil, then simmer on low with salt about 40 minutes until tender. Season.
Prick the sausages, cook in 1/4 inch water in a skillet about 10 minutes until the water is gone and they brown; cool and slice into 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Crisp the salt pork or bacon in the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, 5 to 8 minutes; lift out, leaving the fat.
Cook the second onion in the fat over medium 8 to 10 minutes, then add garlic, tomatoes and paprika for 3 minutes.
Add stock, wine, sausages, pork and 3 tablespoons mint and simmer about 10 minutes.
Add the beans, cover and simmer about 10 minutes, adding stock if dry. Season and garnish with more mint.

title: Mediterranean Vegetable Ragout on a Bed of Polenta
ingredients: 2 medium eggplants, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 scant cup olive oil, or as needed
2 red or green bell peppers, seeded and diced
1/2 pound cremini or white mushrooms, left whole if small, halved or quartered if large
3 large or 4 medium tomatoes, peeled, seeded, and diced
method: Salt the eggplant cubes in a colander for 30 minutes, then wipe off the salt.
Sauté the eggplant in two batches in 3 tablespoons oil each over medium-high heat, 6 to 8 minutes, until tender; set aside in a bowl.
Cook the onions in 2 tablespoons oil about 15 minutes until soft and pale gold, add garlic for 2 minutes, and add to the bowl.
Cook the peppers and zucchini in 3 tablespoons oil 5 to 8 minutes until soft; add to the bowl.
Sauté the mushrooms in 2 to 3 tablespoons oil about 5 minutes, then return all the vegetables to the pan.
Add the tomatoes and cook on low about 15 minutes until melted together. Season and stir in the basil (keeps 2 days chilled).
Serve over polenta.

title: Basic Polenta
ingredients: 1 cup medium- or coarse-grind cornmeal (not instant)
method: Whisk the cold water, salt and cornmeal together in a large saucepan.
Bring slowly to a boil over medium heat, whisking now and then.
As soon as it boils, turn the heat to low and simmer about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy and no longer gritty.
Stir in the butter and Parmesan and serve warm; add hot water as needed to keep it soft.
For firm polenta, spread on an oiled rimmed sheet, chill at least 2 hours, then cut and bake, fry or grill.

title: Pork Loin Glazed with Pomegranate and Orange
ingredients: 1 3-pound boneless pork roast, or 2 1 1/2-pound pork tenderloins
2 tablespoons pomegranate syrup or pomegranate molasses
3 tablespoons pomegranate syrup or pomegranate molasses
method: Put the pork in a nonaluminum container.
Stir together the spice-paste ingredients; set aside 2 tablespoons and rub the rest over the pork. Refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
Let the meat sit at room temperature 30 minutes before cooking.
Whisk the basting-sauce ingredients with the reserved 2 tablespoons paste; hold back 1/4 cup for serving.
Heat a broiler or grill and cook the pork not too close to the heat, basting and turning often, to 140°F: 20 to 30 minutes for a loin, 5 to 8 minutes per side for tenderloins.
Rest 10 minutes, slice thinly and spoon the reserved sauce over.

title: Stuffed Roasted Squab
ingredients: 2 sweet Italian sausages, casings removed, crumbled
2 tablespoons grated pecorino or Parmesan cheese
1/2 teaspoon salt, or more to taste
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, or more to taste
4 thin slices pancetta or prosciutto with some fat
1 cup sweet wine such as vin santo or sherry, or more as needed
method: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rinse and dry the birds and oil a baking pan.
Chop the hearts and livers and mix with the sausage, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, cheese and parsley.
Bind with the butter, salt, pepper and egg, adding more crumbs if too wet. Stuff the birds and sew closed.
Season the birds, wrap in pancetta or prosciutto, set in the pan, scatter with rosemary and sage and drizzle with olive oil.
Roast 45 minutes, basting with the wine; remove the pancetta and roast 10 minutes more until golden.
Remove the thread, halve lengthwise, and serve on warm plates with the pan juices.

title: Salmon with Soy, Ginger, and Sake
ingredients: 1 tablespoon grated peeled fresh ginger, or more to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Combine stock, sake, soy, 1 tablespoon ginger and garlic in a saucepan and boil gently 8 to 10 minutes until reduced by half.
Add more ginger to taste and whisk in butter if using (sauce keeps 5 days chilled; add butter at serving).
Brush the salmon with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Heat a broiler or grill and cook the fish 3 to 4 minutes per side, basting with some sauce, until nearly opaque in the centre.
Bring the remaining sauce to a simmer and pour over the fish to serve.

title: Lamb Shish Kebabs
ingredients: 2 teaspoons dried oregano or chopped fresh thyme
Pinch hot pepper such as Aleppo pepper, cayenne, hot paprika, or hot pimentón de la Vera (optional)
2 pounds tender lamb, preferably from the leg, well trimmed and cut across the grain into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 red onion, cut into squares or quarter-round slices
2 red or green bell peppers, seeded and cut into squares
4 small tomatoes, halved, or 8 to 12 whole cherry tomatoes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Mix the grated onion, garlic, herbs and spices, whisk in the oil and season with salt.
Set aside 2 tablespoons for basting; toss the lamb with the rest and refrigerate overnight.
Heat a broiler or grill. Thread the lamb on skewers with onion and pepper pieces (or put vegetables on their own skewers), leaving small gaps.
Put the tomatoes on separate skewers. Brush all vegetables with oil and season.
Grill the lamb 8 to 12 minutes total, turning and basting, until browned but still pink inside.
Grill the vegetables about 5 minutes, turning once, until tender.

title: Italian Meatball and Vegetable Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh breadcrumbs, soaked in water and squeezed dry
3 spring onions, chopped, or 1 large onion, chopped
2 cups fresh or canned diced plum tomatoes, drained
2 bunches spinach, stemmed, washed, drained, and cut into 1/2-inch strips
1 1/2 pounds fresh favas, shelled (about 1 1/4 cups), blanched, and peeled
1 pound English peas, shelled (about 1 cup), blanched
1 1/2 cups pasta shells cooked al dente (optional)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup grated Parmesan or grana cheese
method: Mix the meat, soaked breadcrumbs, onion and cheese if using, egg, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cook a hazelnut-size test ball, taste and adjust seasoning, then roll the rest into 1-inch balls on a waxed-paper-lined sheet.
Brown the pancetta in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat about 8 minutes; lift out.
Cook the onions, carrots and celery in the drippings 8 to 10 minutes until soft, then return the pancetta.
Add broth and tomatoes, bring to a gentle boil, cover and simmer on low 30 minutes.
Add the meatballs and simmer 10 minutes, then the spinach, favas, peas and pasta if using for 10 minutes more.
Season. If not using pasta, ladle the soup over toasted bread in warm bowls; top with grated cheese.

title: Roast Leg of Lamb with Olives and Orange
ingredients: 1 cup pitted chopped Niçoise or Kalamata olives
method: Process the olives, garlic, orange zest, sage, anchovy and pepper to a paste; keep 2 tablespoons for an optional sauce.
Open out the lamb, flatten it and trim gristle. Spread with the paste, roll up and tie at 1- to 2-inch intervals.
Cut a few slits and tuck in the garlic slivers. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Brown the lamb on all sides in a lightly oiled pan over high heat, 8 to 10 minutes, then move to a roasting pan with the wine.
Roast, basting with the wine, to 120°F for rare (45 minutes to 1 hour) or 130°F for medium (8 to 10 minutes longer).
Rest at least 10 minutes before slicing.
For a sauce, boil the broth and whisk in the reserved paste. Serve the lamb with pan juices and sauce.

title: Osso Buco with Mushrooms and Tomatoes
ingredients: 1 cup dry Marsala or dry red wine
1 ounce dry porcini, soaked in hot water to cover for 30 minutes
1 pound cremini mushrooms, stemmed and sliced or quartered
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Brown the veal shanks in the oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat, 6 to 8 minutes; move to a Dutch oven.
Cook the onions in 3 tablespoons butter over medium heat about 8 minutes until translucent and add to the veal.
Whisk the broth, Marsala and tomato paste, pour over, bring to a gentle boil, cover and braise on low 1 hour.
Meanwhile strain the soaked porcini through cheesecloth, saving the liquid, and chop them.
Sauté the cremini in the remaining butter over high heat about 5 minutes until they release their juices; stir in the porcini and liquid.
Add the mushrooms to the veal and braise 30 minutes to 1 hour more until tender. Season and serve.

title: Rustic Paella
ingredients: 5 tablespoons olive oil, or more as needed
3 cups peeled, seeded, and diced tomatoes (canned are fine)
2 teaspoons sweet paprika or pimentón de la Vera (Spanish smoked paprika)
2 cups Spanish short-grain rice such as Bomba or Calasparra
5 cups chicken broth, or more as needed
1 cup cooked peas, lima beans, chickpeas, or white beans
3 dozen clams or mussels, scrubbed and mussels debearded
White wine or water for steaming clams
method: Mash the garlic, oregano, pepper and salt with the vinegar, whisk in 5 tablespoons extra virgin oil, rub over the chicken and refrigerate overnight.
Simmer the 1/4 cup wine, take off the heat, add saffron and steep 10 minutes.
Brown the chicken in batches in 3 tablespoons oil over high heat, 8 to 10 minutes; set aside and wipe the pan.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat about 10 minutes, then the tomatoes, garlic and paprika 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice over low heat about 3 minutes, then add 5 cups broth and the saffron wine; boil gently, then simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook about 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed; add peas and shrimp and cook about 5 minutes more, adding broth if needed. Cover.
Steam the clams and mussels in 1 inch of wine or water, covered over medium-high heat, 3 to 5 minutes, moving them to the paella as they open; discard any unopened after 10 minutes.
Let the paella stand 10 minutes before serving.

title: Moroccan Lamb Barbecue
ingredients: 1 6-pound leg of lamb (weight with bone), boned and butterflied, or 12 loin lamb chops, or 2 1/2 pounds boneless leg of lamb, trimmed and cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
6 tablespoons olive oil or unsalted butter, melted, plus 1 tablespoon oil for coating the lamb
method: Mix the onion, garlic, spices, herbs, lemon juice and 1/2 cup oil into a charmoula; set a quarter aside, covered and chilled, for basting.
Trim the lamb of fat and sinew, rub with the remaining charmoula and refrigerate overnight.
Bring the meat to room temperature and remove from the marinade. Heat a broiler or grill.
Whisk 6 tablespoons oil or melted butter into the reserved charmoula.
For a butterflied leg, brush with 1 tablespoon oil and cook, turning once and basting, to 120°F rare (8 to 10 minutes per side), 130°F medium (10 to 15) or 140°F well done (15 to 18).
For chops, cook 4 to 6 minutes per side; for kebabs, about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
protein: leg of lamb, chops or kebabs

title: Duck with Sausage and Lentils
ingredients: 1 5-pound duck, neck, feet, wings, and excess fat removed
2 cups green or brown lentils (preferably Italian or French)
1 1/2 pounds mild Italian sausage with fennel
1 cup dry red wine (such as Syrah)
1 cup beef, poultry, or duck stock
Salt and lots of freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 450°F. Pound the garlic, ground fennel, chopped rosemary, salt and pepper to a paste and spread over the duck inside and out.
Put the rosemary sprigs in the cavity, prick the skin all over and roast on a rack about 1 hour until tender. Cut into portions or pull the meat into large pieces.
Bring the lentils and water to a boil, add salt, cover and simmer on low until tender but firm: 30 to 40 minutes for green, 15 to 40 for brown.
Prick the sausages and brown in the oil over high heat 5 to 7 minutes; set aside.
Cook onions, carrots and celery in the pan about 10 minutes, then add garlic, rosemary and fennel and cook on low about 5 minutes.
Combine duck, lentils, sausages, vegetables, wine and stock in a heavy pot and cook over medium heat about 20 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and plenty of pepper and serve hot.

title: Pork Chili Verde
ingredients: 3 pounds pork shoulder or butt, cut into 1 1/2- to 2-inch cubes
4 tablespoons vegetable oil or lard, or more as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 7-ounce can whole or diced roasted green chiles
1/4 cup chopped fresh coriander (cilantro) plus additional for garnish
1 to 2 tablespoons red or white wine vinegar (optional)
method: Mix the oregano and spices, rub over the pork and marinate overnight in the fridge or 1 to 2 hours at room temperature.
Brown the pork in batches in 2 tablespoons oil over high heat, seasoning with salt and pepper, 8 to 10 minutes per batch.
In a stew pot, cook the onions in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat about 10 minutes, add garlic for 2 minutes, then return the pork.
Puree the green chiles, tomatoes, tomatillos and cilantro and stir into the pot with the stock.
Bring to a gentle boil, cover and simmer on low 1 1/2 to 2 hours until the pork is tender.
Season with salt, pepper and vinegar if you like. Serve warm with extra cilantro and sour cream.

title: Korean Short Ribs
ingredients: 3 pounds meaty English short ribs, each rib about 3 inches long
1/4 cup sesame seeds, toasted and ground
method: Score the meat deeply every 1/2 inch without cutting it off the bone.
Rub the sugar and sesame oil all over and into the cuts; let stand 30 minutes at room temperature.
Mix the soy sauce, green onions, garlic, sesame seeds, flour, pepper flakes and ginger and rub into the ribs.
Let stand 1 hour more at room temperature (or up to 4 hours chilled, then bring back to room temperature).
Heat a broiler or grill and cook the ribs, turning often, 4 to 5 minutes per side, about 20 minutes total, until tender.

title: Seared Tuna with Rosemary, Garlic, and Hot Pepper
ingredients: 4 6-ounce slices sashimi-grade tuna (preferably ahi), 3/4 to 1 inch thick
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon red pepper flakes, or more to taste
method: Season the tuna with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat and sear the tuna, turning once, until browned, 6 to 8 minutes total. Keep warm under foil.
Add the wine, stock, rosemary, garlic and 1 tablespoon pepper flakes to the pan and boil over high heat 5 to 8 minutes until reduced by half.
Season with salt, pepper and more pepper flakes.
Return the tuna to the pan for about 1 minute to coat with sauce, and serve at once.
wines: Zinfandel / Primitivo (light, fruity, about 12% alcohol, slightly chilled)

title: Pasta with Artichokes, Pancetta, Mushrooms, and Peas
ingredients: 1/2 cup water, or more as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 cups sliced mushrooms (any combination of button, cremini, chanterelles, or fresh porcini)
2/3 pound pancetta sliced 1/4 inch thick, unrolled and cut crosswise into 1/4-inch strips
1 pound dried garganelli or fresh fettuccine
method: Squeeze most of the lemon into a bowl of cold water. Trim each artichoke down to the heart, scoop out the choke, slice 1/4 inch thick and drop into the lemon water.
Drain and cook the slices in 4 tablespoons oil over medium heat with a squeeze of lemon and 1/2 cup water, stirring, about 10 minutes until just tender. Season.
Sauté the mushrooms in 3 tablespoons oil over high heat about 3 minutes; set aside.
Cook the pancetta in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat 5 to 8 minutes until starting to brown; add to the mushrooms, keeping the fat in the pan.
Put a large pot of salted water on to boil.
Add 4 tablespoons oil to the pan and cook the onions about 8 minutes; add artichokes, mushrooms, pancetta, garlic, peas and thyme and heat through. Season.
Cook the pasta until al dente (or tender if fresh), drain and toss with the vegetables over low heat for a minute or two.
Serve hot sprinkled with Parmesan and parsley.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 4 tablespoons olive oil, bacon fat, or lard
2 green bell peppers, seeded and chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 to 1 1/2 pounds linguiça or polish sausage
1 small jar dried beef, cut into 1/2-inch strips (optional)
method: Soak the beans overnight in cold water covering them by 4 inches; drain.
Cook the onions and peppers in 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat about 8 minutes, then garlic 2 minutes; season.
Add the beans and water to cover by 1 1/2 inches, bring to a gentle boil, cover and simmer on low 30 to 40 minutes until tender. Drain excess liquid and puree 1 to 2 cups of beans to thicken.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Brown the pork in batches in 2 tablespoons oil over high heat, about 8 minutes per batch, and add to the beans.
Brown the chorizo and linguiça in the drippings 5 to 7 minutes, cut into large pieces and add to the pot.
Deglaze the pan with orange juice and wine and add to the pot with the dried beef if using.
Cover and bake about 1 hour until the pork is tender.

title: Barbecued Chicken Sandwiches
ingredients: 3 tablespoons chili powder (such as Grandma’s or Gebhardt’s)
1/2 cup fresh orange juice, or 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (optional)
1 tablespoon freshly ground black pepper, or more to taste
Cayenne pepper or hot sauce to taste
6 bone-in or boneless chicken breast halves
method: Make the barbecue sauce (see Basic Barbecue Sauce) and warm it.
Heat the broiler. Set aside 1/2 cup sauce for basting and 1 cup for serving; save the rest for another meal.
Broil the chicken, basting now and then and turning once, about 5 minutes per side (3 if boneless), until the juices run clear.
Shred the meat (or slice boneless breasts 1/4 inch thick).
Dip the chicken in the reserved sauce, pile onto rolls and serve with the remaining warm sauce.

title: Basic Barbecue Sauce
ingredients: 3 tablespoons chili powder (such as Grandma’s or Gebhardt’s)
1/2 cup fresh orange juice, or 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (optional)
1 tablespoon freshly ground black pepper, or more to taste
Cayenne pepper or hot sauce to taste
method: Mix the mustard powder, chili powder and ginger with a little vinegar into a smooth paste, then whisk in the rest of the vinegar.
Pour into a saucepan and whisk in the tomato puree, Worcestershire, brown sugar, citrus juice if using and 1 tablespoon pepper.
Bring to a boil over medium heat and simmer 5 minutes, thinning with a little water if too thick.
Season with more pepper, cayenne and salt.
Refrigerate covered for up to 2 months; rewarm before using.

title: Hazelnut Torte with Coffee Buttercream
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter two 9-inch round pans, line with parchment and butter the paper.
Toast the hazelnuts 10 to 15 minutes, rub off the skins in a rough towel, then grind finely with 1/4 cup sugar.
Whip the egg whites with salt to soft peaks, then add the remaining 1 cup sugar a spoonful at a time until stiff and glossy.
Beat the yolks until light, add vanilla and stir in a quarter of the whites.
Fold in the nut mixture and flour, then the remaining whites.
Divide between the pans and bake 30 to 40 minutes until springy. Cool 10 minutes, turn out, peel off the paper and cool fully.
Sandwich the layers with about 3/4 cup buttercream, cover top and sides with the rest, decorate with whole hazelnuts and refrigerate.

title: Coffee Buttercream with Egg Whites
ingredients: 3/4 pound (3 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into small pieces
4 tablespoons very strong coffee, or 2 or 3 tablespoons instant espresso dissolved in 2 tablespoons hot water
method: Stir the sugar, water and corn syrup over high heat until dissolved, then boil without stirring, washing down crystals with a wet brush.
Cook to soft-ball stage, 238°F, and pour at once into a glass measuring cup.
Whisk the egg whites until foamy. With the mixer stopped, add a third of the syrup, then mix briefly on low; repeat twice.
Beat on high until satiny, stiff and completely cool.
Beat in the butter piece by piece until smooth, then the coffee. If it separates, chill 15 minutes and beat again.
Chill until firm enough to spread.

title: Coffee Buttercream with Egg Yolks
ingredients: 3/4 pound (3 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into small pieces
4 tablespoons very strong coffee, or 2 or 3 tablespoons instant espresso dissolved in 2 tablespoons hot water
method: Boil the sugar, water and cream of tartar until the syrup spins a thread, 236 to 238°F, and pour into a glass measuring cup.
Whisk the yolks until fluffy. With the mixer stopped add a third of the syrup and mix briefly on low; repeat twice.
Beat on high until the yolks are thick, pale and cool.
Beat in the butter one piece at a time, then the coffee.
Chill until firm enough to spread.

title: Citrus Marmalade Tart
ingredients: 12 tablespoons (1 1/2 sticks) chilled unsalted butter, diced
5 tablespoons ice water, or as needed
3 to 4 large navel oranges, or 6 blood oranges, or 4 blood oranges and 4 Meyer lemons
4 tablespoons (1/2 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature
3 tablespoons Grand Marnier or other orange liqueur
2 tablespoons Grand Marnier or other orange liqueur
method: Pulse flour, sugar and salt, add the butter and pulse to coarse meal, then add ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough holds. Shape into two discs, one larger, and chill at least 1 hour.
Remove and finely chop about 1 cup zest, cut off the pith and free about 3 cups of segments from their membranes.
Simmer the fruit, zest, sugar, lemon juice and water about 20 minutes until thick, stirring now and then; cool.
Roll the larger disc between parchment to a 13-inch circle, fit into a 9-inch pie plate or 10-inch tart pan and chill. Heat the oven to 450°F.
Whisk sugar and cornstarch, beat in the butter until fluffy, add eggs one at a time, then fold in the marmalade and 3 tablespoons liqueur.
Roll the second disc to a 12 x 9-inch rectangle and cut 1-inch strips. Fill the crust, moisten the edge and weave a lattice on top; trim and pinch to seal.
Bake 10 minutes, then at 350°F about 25 minutes more until set and lightly colored.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, add sugar and liqueur and beat until thick. Serve the tart warm or at room temperature with the cream.
wines: Late-harvest white (raisined, passito, Tokaji, Vin Santo, Muscat)

title: Lemony Ricotta Soufflé Cake with Raspberry Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 cup fine dry breadcrumbs, or as needed
2 tablespoons whipping cream or sour cream
method: Heat the oven to 325°F. Butter a 9-inch springform pan, coat with breadcrumbs and tap out the excess.
Beat the sugar and yolks until very thick and pale, then on low beat in ricotta, flour, cream, vanilla and lemon zest. Add pine nuts if using.
Whip the whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl, stir in a quarter, then fold in the rest until no streaks remain.
Spoon into the pan, leaving an inch of room to rise.
Bake about 50 minutes until set but still slightly wobbly. Cool about 1 hour in the oven with the door ajar, or on a rack.
Loosen the sides with a knife, unclip the pan and serve in wedges with raspberry sauce.

title: Raspberry Sauce
ingredients: 1 12-ounce package frozen whole raspberries (not in syrup), thawed
method: Puree the thawed raspberries in a blender or food processor.
Push through a fine sieve to remove the seeds.
Whisk in framboise to taste if using. Keeps up to 2 days covered in the fridge.

title: Caramel-Coated Cream Puffs
serves: Makes about 18 small or 12 medium puffs
ingredients: 7 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces
method: Heat the oven to 400°F and line 2 baking sheets with parchment.
Boil the water, milk, butter and salt, add the flour and sugar all at once and stir until the dough dries and leaves the sides of the pan.
Beat in the eggs one at a time with a mixer until smooth and glossy. Pipe or spoon 1-inch mounds onto the sheets and sprinkle with almonds.
Bake 15 minutes, then 350°F about 10 minutes until golden. Turn off the oven and let them dry inside with the door ajar.
For the pastry cream, scald the milk. Beat eggs and sugar until thick, whisk in the flour, then slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Return to the pan and stir over medium heat about 5 minutes until it boils and thickens. Add vanilla and cool over ice water.
Pipe the cream into each puff through a small hole.
Dissolve the sugar in the orange juice and water over medium-high heat, then simmer, swirling and brushing down the sides, until golden brown.
Dip the top of each puff in the hot caramel with tongs and cool about 10 minutes on a rack. Serve within 6 hours.

title: Creamy Caramel Sauce
method: Warm the cream to a bare simmer and keep it hot.
Moisten the sugar with the orange juice in a small heavy pan and cook over high heat, swirling and brushing down the sides, until golden brown.
Slowly pour in the hot cream, stirring constantly (it will bubble up hard), and bring to a boil.
Off the heat, whisk in the butter and Grand Marnier if using. Serve warm.
Keeps a week refrigerated; rewarm in a double boiler or briefly in the microwave.

title: Coconut Panna Cotta with Mango Sauce
method: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let soften about 10 minutes. Chill a pitcher.
Whisk the coconut milk, cream, sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring often.
Off the heat, stir in the gelatin until dissolved, then the vanilla.
Pour into the cold pitcher set in ice water and stir now and then 15 to 20 minutes until slightly thicker than heavy cream.
Pour into five or six 4-ounce cups and chill at least 4 hours (up to 2 days).
Run a knife around each cup, unmold onto plates and spoon mango puree around.
wines: Late-harvest white (Muscat, Sémillon or Chenin Blanc)

title: Mango Puree
method: Peel the mangos and cut the flesh into small pieces.
Puree in a food processor, then add 3 tablespoons honey and the salt and blend again.
Add more honey to taste. Keeps 1 day chilled; serve at room temperature.

title: Tartufo Budino
ingredients: 24 amarene cherries soaked in kirsch or brandy (sour cherries)
method: Brush six 5-ounce ramekins with the melted butter, dust with 1 tablespoon sugar and put 4 cherries in each.
Melt the chocolate with 14 tablespoons butter in a double boiler, then stir in 8 tablespoons sugar, vanilla and salt.
Warm the beaten yolks with a little chocolate mixture, then whisk them into the chocolate.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Whip the whites with 2 tablespoons sugar to medium peaks and fold into the chocolate.
Fill the ramekins (can be chilled up to 5 hours) and sprinkle with the last tablespoon of sugar.
Set in a baking pan with 1 inch of hot water and bake 20 to 30 minutes until puffed and crackly on top but still wobbly inside.
Serve warm with whipped cream.
